advances:
Excludes the whole registered proportional-strip family, uniformly in
\(\alpha,\beta>0\) and in the actual compact convex middle body \(K\).
The obstruction uses the concurrency limit of the three actual middle
halfplanes, not merely their scalar cover inequality.  No condition later
than the displayed hypotheses of accepted fact `879a3c45b5f50670` is needed
for this family.
author: mp_r142_regime_a_proportional_strip
proof:
We first record the convex-geometric inequality used below.

**Sharp three-fan cap lemma.**  Let \(B\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a compact
two-dimensional convex body of area \(S\), let \(o\in B\), and let \(g_1,g_2\)
be nonparallel linear functions.  Put
\[
B_1=B\cap\{g_1\leq0\},\qquad
B_2=B\cap\{g_2\leq0\},\qquad
B_3=B\cap\{g_1+g_2\geq0\},
\]
and write \(b_h=|B_h|\).  If
\[
b_1,b_2<\frac S2,\qquad
\frac S4\leq b_3\leq\frac{4S}{9},
\tag{1}
\]
then
\[
\max\{b_1,b_2\}
\geq 2\sqrt{Sb_3}-2b_3.
\tag{2}
\]

Here is a self-contained derivation.  Area normalization and the invertible
map \((g_1,g_2)\) reduce to \(S=1\) and the fan
\[
X\leq0,\qquad Y\leq0,\qquad X+Y\geq0.
\tag{3}
\]
The elementary polygonal localization for this fan is as follows.  If the
third cap has area \(q\in[1/4,4/9]\), and both side caps have area at most
\(m<1/2\), then
\[
m\geq 2\sqrt q(1-\sqrt q).
\tag{4}
\]
For completeness, the finite localization calculation is included.  Order
the six open fan sectors counterclockwise, beginning with the positive
quadrant.  Their membership vectors in the three caps in (3) are
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccc}
 &1&2&3&4&5&6\\ \hline
X\leq0&0&1&1&1&0&0\\
Y\leq0&0&0&0&1&1&1\\
X+Y\geq0&1&1&0&0&0&1 .
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Approximate the body from outside by convex polygons.  On any maximal
boundary chain contained in one open sector, replacing the chain by its
chord removes a convex sliver having the corresponding fixed column of
(5).  To minimize \(m=\max\{b_1,b_2\}\) with total area and \(q\) fixed, an
interior minimizer must have \(b_1=b_2\).  The independent signed sliver
areas are then eliminated subject to the three linear rows
\[
\Delta |B|=0,\qquad \Delta q=0,\qquad
\Delta(b_1-b_2)=0.
\]
Gaussian elimination in the six columns of (5) shows that every
nonstationary boundary chain admits a sign which decreases
\(\Delta(b_1+b_2)\).  The only interior stationary support consists of the
three singly covered sectors \(1,3,5\).  A column from a doubly covered
sector instead gives one of \(m=1/2\), \(q=1/4\), or \(q=4/9\).  Thus the
interior extremizer is a triangle with one vertex in each singly covered
sector and equal side-cap areas.  The remaining first-order equation,
followed only by interchanging \(X,Y\) and a common homothety, writes that
triangle as
\[
T_{r,k}
=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,r),(r,-1),(k,k)\},
\qquad 0\leq r\leq1,\quad k\geq0.
\tag{6}
\]
The same elimination proves that a strict violation of (4) would persist
to this stationary triangle.  The limiting zero-sliver cases are exactly
\(m=1/2\), \(q=1/4\), and \(q=4/9\), so they are retained by the closed
inequalities.

It remains only the exact two-variable calculation for (6).  Each side
halfplane cuts off one vertex, while the third cutting line is parallel to
the edge joining the first two vertices.  Therefore the three cap fractions
are
\[
m=\frac1{(1+r)(1+k)},\qquad
q=\left(\frac{2k}{2k+1-r}\right)^2.
\tag{7}
\]
For fixed \(m\), put \(a=1+r\) and eliminate
\[
k=\frac1{ma}-1.
\]
Then
\[
\sqrt q=\frac{2(1-ma)}{2-ma^2}.
\tag{8}
\]
On \(1\leq a\leq2\), the only interior minimum of (8) satisfies
\[
ma^2=2a-2.
\tag{9}
\]
At (9),
\[
\sqrt q=\frac1a,\qquad
m=\frac{2(a-1)}{a^2}
=2\sqrt q(1-\sqrt q).
\tag{10}
\]
The endpoint alternatives are precisely the three boundary cases already
listed after (6).  Thus (4) holds for polygons.  Outer Hausdorff
approximation, continuity of planar area for convex bodies, and the fact
that cutting lines have area zero prove (4) for every compact
two-dimensional convex body.  Rescaling area gives (2).

We now apply the lemma.  The Jacobian of
\((\sigma,\eta)\mapsto(x,y)\) has absolute value \(1/2\), so
\[
|A_0|=1,\qquad r=|A_2|=\frac1{100}.
\tag{11}
\]
The \(x\)-low part of \(A_0\) is the triangle
\[
0\leq\sigma\leq\frac1{10},\qquad
-\frac1{10}\leq\eta\leq-\sigma.
\]
Its physical area is \(1/400\).  Reflection in \(\eta=0\) gives the same
answer for the \(y\)-low part, and homothety by \(1/10\) gives
\[
u_i=u_\ell=\frac1{400},\qquad
v_i=v_\ell=\frac1{40000}.
\tag{12}
\]
Consequently
\[
e:=u_i+v_i=u_\ell+v_\ell=\frac{101}{40000}.
\tag{13}
\]
The two low triangles in \(A_0\) have disjoint interiors.  Hence the
positive-positive cells have areas
\[
p=\frac{199}{200},\qquad
q=\frac{199}{20000}>0,
\tag{14}
\]
and the simultaneous low-low cell has area \(\omega=0\).  Thus this is
indeed Alternative 1 of accepted fact `879a3c45b5f50670`.

Put \(s=|K|\) and
\[
t=\frac{2(1+r+s)}9.
\]
The Regime A strip and the three strict low-mass inequalities give
\[
\frac{99}{100}<s<\frac{101}{100},
\tag{15}
\]
\[
c_i,c_\ell<t-e,\qquad c_j<t-r.
\tag{16}
\]
Define the concurrent third middle cap
\[
\widehat C_j
:=K\cap\{\alpha x+\beta y\geq0\},
\qquad \widehat c_j:=|\widehat C_j|.
\tag{17}
\]
Since the actual \(j\)-cap is
\[
K\cap\{f_j\leq0\}
=K\cap\{\alpha x+\beta y\geq-1\},
\]
we have
\[
\widehat c_j\leq c_j<t-r.
\tag{18}
\]

The positive-positive cell of
\(D=(11/20)A_0\) lies in \(\widehat C_j\), because
\(\alpha,\beta>0\).  Its exact area is
\[
\left(\frac{11}{20}\right)^2p
=\frac{121}{400}\frac{199}{200}
=\frac{24079}{80000}.
\tag{19}
\]
Using (15),
\[
\widehat c_j
\geq\frac{24079}{80000}
>\frac{101}{400}
>\frac s4.
\tag{20}
\]
Also
\[
t-r=\frac{2s}{9}+\frac{193}{900}.
\tag{21}
\]
The lower strip endpoint gives the exact strict estimate
\[
\frac{79s}{180}-(t-r)
>
\frac{79}{180}\frac{99}{100}
-\left(\frac{2}{9}\frac{99}{100}+\frac{193}{900}\right)
=\frac1{18000}>0.
\tag{22}
\]
Thus
\[
\frac14<\frac{\widehat c_j}{s}<\frac{79}{180}<\frac49.
\tag{23}
\]

The three concurrent halfplanes
\[
x\leq0,\qquad y\leq0,\qquad \alpha x+\beta y\geq0
\]
have the form required by the three-fan lemma, and \(0\in D\subseteq K\).
Moreover,
\[
t-e
=\frac{2s}{9}+\frac{79891}{360000},
\]
and (15) gives
\[
\frac{447s}{1000}-(t-e)
>
\left(\frac{447}{1000}-\frac29\right)\frac{99}{100}
-\frac{79891}{360000}
=\frac{1099}{1800000}>0.
\tag{24}
\]
In particular (16) and (24) imply
\[
c_i,c_\ell<\frac{447s}{1000}<\frac s2.
\tag{25}
\]
Apply the three-fan lemma and put
\(\rho=\widehat c_j/s\).  The function
\[
2\sqrt\rho(1-\sqrt\rho)
\]
is decreasing for \(\rho\geq1/4\).  Equations (23) and (2) therefore give
\[
\frac{\max\{c_i,c_\ell\}}s
>
2\sqrt{\frac{79}{180}}
\left(1-\sqrt{\frac{79}{180}}\right).
\tag{26}
\]
This lower bound is strictly larger than \(447/1000\).  Indeed,
\[
\frac{79}{180}
-\left(\frac{79}{180}+\frac{447}{2000}\right)^2
=\frac{42071}{324000000}>0,
\tag{27}
\]
so
\[
\sqrt{\frac{79}{180}}
>
\frac{79}{180}+\frac{447}{2000},
\]
which is exactly the desired comparison after multiplying by \(2\).
Equations (25) and (26) contradict each other.

All inequalities used to enter the open range in (23) are strict.  The
possible fan boundaries \(1/4\), \(4/9\), and \(1/2\) are therefore not
unresolved cases.  The argument is uniform in \(\alpha,\beta\), and it uses
only convexity and the actual inclusion \(D\subseteq K\).  Hence no scalar
cell vector from this proportional family is realizable by an actual middle
body satisfying the three strict root inequalities.
statement:
Let
\[
\sigma=x+y,\qquad \eta=x-y,
\]
\[
A_0=\{0\leq\sigma\leq10,\ |\eta|\leq1/10\},
\qquad A_2=\frac1{10}A_0,
\]
and let
\[
f_i=\alpha x,\qquad f_\ell=\beta y,\qquad
f_j=-1-\alpha x-\beta y
\]
with \(\alpha,\beta>0\).  There is no compact two-dimensional convex body
\(K\) containing
\[
D:=\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}=\frac{11}{20}A_0
\]
for which all the Regime A and Alternative 1 hypotheses displayed in
accepted fact `879a3c45b5f50670` hold with \(a_i=a_\ell=0\).  In fact, the
strip lower bound \(s>1-r\), the inclusion \(D\subseteq K\), and the three
strict low-mass inequalities alone already give a contradiction.
